identification.summary: Citrine Sleet is Microsoft's name for a North Korea-based actor that goes after financial institutions, especially organizations and individuals that manage cryptocurrency, for financial gain [S1]. Its usual methods are fake cryptocurrency trading sites, fake job applications and weaponized wallet or trading apps. Its most common trojan is AppleJeus [S1]. In August 2024 Microsoft attributed, with medium confidence, exploitation of a Chromium zero-day (CVE-2024-7971) to Citrine Sleet. The intrusion chained a Windows kernel exploit and deployed the FudModule rootkit [S1]. Overlapping vendor clusters are linked to the 2023 3CX cascading supply-chain compromise (Mandiant UNC4736) [S2], to 2024 poisoned PyPI packages (Unit 42 Gleaming Pisces) [S3], and to the October 2024 Radiant Capital theft of about $50M [S5].
identification.firstObserved: Trojanized AppleJeus applications have been in use since 2018, per the US government advisory as reported [S4]. Unit 42 says Gleaming Pisces has been active since at least 2018 [S3]. Microsoft gives no first-observed date [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Citrine Sleet. Microsoft says other security companies track this actor as AppleJeus, Labyrinth Chollima, UNC4736 and Hidden Cobra [S1]. Microsoft's naming map also lists Storm-0139 and Storm-1222 [S8]. MITRE tracks the group as AppleJeus (G1049) [S7]. Unit 42 equates Gleaming Pisces with Citrine Sleet [S3]. Mandiant links UNC4736 to AppleJeus with moderate confidence [S2]. Microsoft's December 2022 DEV-0139 report (Telegram lures against crypto investment funds) is listed here as a probable predecessor designation; the naming-map entry Storm-0139 suggests this, but no cited source explicitly confirms it [S6][S8]. 'Hidden Cobra' is a broad US government term for DPRK activity, not a precise cluster name.

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Microsoft says Citrine Sleet is based in North Korea and reportedly linked to Bureau 121 of the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) [S1]. Press reporting of Mandiant's Radiant Capital findings describes UNC4736 as aligned to the RGB [S5].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft assesses with high confidence that the CVE-2024-7971 exploitation came from a North Korean actor, and with medium confidence that the actor was Citrine Sleet [S1]. Mandiant assessed with moderate confidence that UNC4736 (3CX) is related to the AppleJeus activity reported by CISA [S2]. As reported by the victim and press, Mandiant assessed with high confidence that the Radiant Capital attack was DPRK-nexus and attributed it to UNC4736 [S5]. Unit 42 assesses with medium confidence that PondRAT belongs to Gleaming Pisces [S3]. FBI, CISA and Treasury attributed AppleJeus malware to North Korean state-sponsored actors (the Lazarus Group) in February 2021 [S4].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and exploit analysis [S1]. Mandiant incident response at 3CX, including a POOLRAT sample matching the AppleJeus CoinGoTrade app [S2]. Unit 42 code, encryption-key and C2 overlaps [S3]. A joint US government malware analysis advisory (AA21-048A) [S4]. Mandiant's Radiant Capital investigation as reported in press [S5].

objectives: Revenue generation for the DPRK through theft of cryptocurrency and other financial assets [S1][S7]. The US government assesses that the modified trading apps are likely a way to get around international sanctions on North Korea [S4]. Unit 42 assesses that the PyPI campaign aimed to reach supply-chain vendors through developer endpoints, and then those vendors' customers [S3].

sectors: Cryptocurrency exchanges, funds, wallets and individuals managing crypto assets [S1][S6]
Decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols and their developers [S5]
Software vendors and supply chains (VoIP software, trading software) [S2]
Software developers via open-source package repositories (PyPI) [S3]
Finance, government, energy, technology and telecommunications (AppleJeus victims, per coverage of the US advisory) [S4]
regions: Global; cryptocurrency-theft targeting in over 30 countries in one year, per the US advisory as reported [S4]
Downstream customers of 3CX, a globally used VoIP software vendor [S2]
targeting.notes: Microsoft notes that one organization targeted in the 2024 Chromium campaign had previously been targeted by Sapphire Sleet [S1]. The US government assessed that North Korean actors like Citrine Sleet will likely keep targeting crypto technology firms, gaming companies and exchanges [S1]. The sector list for 2021 comes from secondary coverage of the CISA advisory, which describes the wider AppleJeus/Lazarus activity [S4].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering through fake trading sites, fake job offers and Telegram contacts posing as trusted peers or former contractors [S1][S5][S6]. Trojanized cryptocurrency trading and wallet apps (AppleJeus; seven named variants, including Celas Trade Pro, JMT Trading and CoinGoTrade) [S4]. Zero-day exploitation: Chromium V8 type confusion CVE-2024-7971 chained with Windows kernel CVE-2024-38106 for sandbox escape, then the FudModule rootkit, which uses direct kernel object manipulation (DKOM) to tamper with kernel security mechanisms [S1]. FudModule is also attributed to Diamond Sleet, and Microsoft suggests the two groups may share it [S1]. Software supply-chain compromise: a trojanized, validly signed X_TRADER installer led to compromise of 3CX's Windows and macOS build environments and a trojanized 3CX Desktop App. Associated tools include VEILEDSIGNAL, TAXHAUL, COLDCAT, SUDDENICON, ICONICSTEALER and POOLRAT [S2]. Cross-platform backdoors for Windows, macOS and Linux, including POOLRAT, its lighter variant PondRAT delivered through poisoned PyPI packages [S3], and the macOS backdoor INLETDRIFT [S5]. Use of compromised developer devices to sign fraudulent multisignature transactions [S5].

campaigns.name: AppleJeus trojanized trading apps
campaigns.summary: Malicious cryptocurrency trading applications appear (Celas Trade Pro and later variants), first delivered through look-alike trading platform websites and later through phishing and social engineering.

campaigns.name: US joint advisory AA21-048A (AppleJeus)
campaigns.summary: FBI, CISA and Treasury publish analysis of seven AppleJeus versions and report cryptocurrency-theft targeting in more than 30 countries in the previous year.

campaigns.name: Trading Technologies website compromise
campaigns.summary: tradingtechnologies[.]com is compromised; it later serves a trojanized, signed X_TRADER installer (Mandiant citing Google TAG).

campaigns.name: DEV-0139 Telegram lures against crypto funds
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports an actor joining Telegram VIP groups, posing as a crypto firm and sending a weaponized Excel fee-structure file that led to a backdoor. The link to Citrine Sleet is probable but not confirmed in cited sources.

campaigns.name: 3CX cascading supply-chain compromise
campaigns.summary: Trojanized X_TRADER on a 3CX employee's machine leads to compromise of 3CX build environments and a trojanized 3CX Desktop App. Mandiant attributes it to UNC4736.

campaigns.name: Chromium zero-day CVE-2024-7971 and FudModule
campaigns.summary: Microsoft identifies exploitation on 19 August 2024. Victims are directed to voyagorclub[.]space, then a kernel sandbox escape and FudModule rootkit follow. Google patches the flaw on 21 August.

campaigns.name: Poisoned PyPI packages delivering PondRAT
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 reports Gleaming Pisces uploading poisoned Python packages that deliver Linux and macOS backdoors.

campaigns.name: Radiant Capital theft (~$50M)
campaigns.summary: After a 11 September 2024 Telegram lure from a fake former contractor delivered INLETDRIFT, compromised developer devices signed fraudulent multisig transactions. Mandiant attributes the theft to UNC4736.

diamond.adversary: DPRK state-sponsored operators, reportedly linked to RGB Bureau 121 [S1]. Clustered by vendors as Citrine Sleet, UNC4736, Gleaming Pisces and Labyrinth Chollima [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.capability: AppleJeus trojanized apps [S4]; Chromium and Windows kernel zero-days with the FudModule rootkit [S1]; supply-chain implants (VEILEDSIGNAL, TAXHAUL, POOLRAT) [S2]; PondRAT [S3]; INLETDRIFT [S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake cryptocurrency trading and wallet websites [S1][S4]. Exploit delivery domain voyagorclub[.]space and weinsteinfrog[.]com [S1]. A compromised legitimate vendor site (tradingtechnologies[.]com) and GitHub-hosted icon files used for C2 resolution [S2]. PyPI packages and C2 domains jdkgradle[.]com and rebelthumb[.]net [S3]. A spoofed contractor website and Telegram accounts [S5].
diamond.victim: Cryptocurrency exchanges, funds, DeFi protocols and individuals [S1][S5][S6]; software vendors and their downstream customers [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Sanctions evasion and revenue generation for the DPRK regime through theft of digital assets [S1][S4].
diamond.technology: Exploits trust in signed software and software update channels [S2], open-source package ecosystems [S3], browser and kernel vulnerabilities [S1], and multisignature wallet-signing workflows on developer endpoints [S5].

gaps: Microsoft's own attribution of the 3CX compromise was not found. The 3CX link to Citrine Sleet rests on Mandiant's UNC4736 cluster (moderate-confidence AppleJeus link) and on Microsoft listing UNC4736 as an alias [S1][S2].
Unit 42's Gleaming Pisces report could not be opened (DNS failure). Its content comes from search-result summaries [S3].
CISA AA21-048A could not be opened (government site blocked). Details come from search-result coverage, including McGuireWoods and other secondary reporting [S4].
Mandiant's Radiant Capital findings are known only through the victim's statement as reported in press. SecurityWeek could not be fetched, and the article's exact date is approximate [S5].
No cited source explicitly confirms that Microsoft's DEV-0139 (December 2022) is Citrine Sleet. The Microsoft blog itself was not opened [S6][S8].
Boundary with Diamond Sleet and Sapphire Sleet: the clusters share FudModule and infrastructure, and some victims overlap. Tool attribution may span actors [S1].
AppleJeus reporting in the 2021 US advisory refers broadly to the 'Lazarus Group'. Its victim-sector list may cover activity beyond the Citrine Sleet cluster [S4].
No public reporting on Citrine Sleet activity in 2025 or 2026 was found in this research pass.
The meaning and scope of Microsoft's Storm-1222 designation are not described in the cited sources [S8].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Key terrain includes developer endpoints, software build environments, update and code-signing chains, open-source package dependencies (PyPI), and the browser and kernel attack surface of Windows workstations [S1][S2][S3]. Personnel reached through Telegram and LinkedIn-style job lures are part of the human terrain [S5][S6]. STEP 2 (effects): One trojanized vendor installer can cascade into downstream supply-chain compromise of widely deployed enterprise software such as VoIP clients [S2]. Zero-day chains can bypass browser sandboxes and kernel defenses [S1]. STEP 3 (adversary template): social-engineering lure (fake job, trusted-contact impersonation, fake trading site) or zero-day watering hole, then cross-platform backdoor (AppleJeus, POOLRAT/PondRAT, INLETDRIFT, VEILEDSIGNAL), then credential and wallet access or build-system tampering [S1][S2][S3][S5]. STEP 4: The MLCOA is continued financially motivated theft from crypto and fintech entities, with no direct targeting of DoD. The MDCOA is a supply-chain implant in software also used by DoD or defense industrial base networks, giving incidental access that could be passed to espionage-focused DPRK units, as in the 3CX case where victims were downstream customers [S2]. Candidate indicators: unexpected child processes or DLL side-loading from signed vendor installers [S2]; installs of newly published or typosquatted PyPI packages on developer hosts [S3]; Chromium renderer crashes followed by kernel-mode tampering of security callbacks [S1]; connections to known C2 such as voyagorclub[.]space, jdkgradle[.]com and rebelthumb[.]net [S1][S3]; and macOS .app files posing as PDFs delivered over Telegram [S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track software bill-of-materials and vendor-compromise alerts, such as trojanized 3CX builds, across DODIN and mission partner networks, because this actor's supply-chain operations can reach DoD users incidentally [S2]. Monitor emergency Chromium and Windows kernel patches, since the 2024 chain was patched within days of discovery [S1]. (2) Authorities: activity is primarily financial theft by a state actor. Coordinate with FBI and Treasury, which have issued joint guidance on AppleJeus, and with law enforcement for any DIB victim [S4]. (3) Mission assurance: harden developer and build environments, enforce package allow-listing for PyPI, and verify code-signing provenance of third-party installers [S2][S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3/DIB CS and commercial vendors. Note that vendor clusters (Citrine Sleet, UNC4736, Gleaming Pisces, Labyrinth Chollima) overlap but are not identical, and tools such as FudModule are shared with Diamond Sleet, so prioritize containment over precise attribution [S1][S2][S3].

provenance.importedSummary: AppleJeus is a North Korean state-sponsored threat group attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau. Associated with the broader Lazarus Group umbrella of actors, AppleJeus has been active since at least 2018 and is closely aligned in resources with TEMP.hermit, another DPRK-affiliated group under the same umbrella. The group’s primary mission is to generate and launder revenue to provide financial support to the government. AppleJeus primarily targets the cryptocurrency industry and is most notably responsible for the 3CX Supply Chain Attack. The group traditionally deploys malicious cryptocurrency software in combination with Phishing. From these compromised environments, it selectively deploys additional backdoors to enable extended operations against high-value financial targets.
